text:
Maya: Quick flag — spotted a mismatch in route selection during the console canary.
Alex: paste the rule objects?
Maya: sure:
```
- match:
    host: "billing.api.acme.com"
    path: "/v1/*"
  service: acme-v1
- match:
    header:
      name: "x-svc-override"
      exact: "billing"
    path: "/v1/*"
  service: acme-billing
```
Maya: expected: request with x-svc-override=billing -> acme-billing. observed: still routed to acme-v1 when host was billing.api.acme.com
Ernie: are we giving host exact a higher score than header exact right now?
Alex: yes, current scoring: host_exact=100, path=80, header_exact=70 (legacy weights).
Ciara: that explains it. I thought header exact should have parity for explicit overrides.
Sam: +1 to parity, but watch out for broad header patterns outranking specific hosts. we need a rule for regex/wildcard caps.
Ernie: proposal: set header_exact=100, header_prefix=75, header_regex=60, capture_penalty=-20 for wildcards. compute total as sum(anchor_weights)+path_score+capture_penalty.
Maya: also want the console to surface a concise breakdown: e.g. "matched because header_exact(100) + path(80) > host_exact(100) + path(60)" — makes debugging faster.
Ciara: telemetry: emit route_eval with { chosen_rule_id, candidate_rule_ids, score_breakdown }. IMPORTANT: do not log header values — only header name and match_kind. redact values.
Alex: I'll open a matcher PR with tests covering host-wildcard vs header-exact and add the console hint change.
Sam: add a unit test for header-regex vs host-exact too, and enforce a max contribution for regex matches so they can't escalate.
Ernie: ops/privacy check: ok if telemetry contains rule ids and scores but no PII. add automated scrub to the pipeline.
Maya: timeline: Alex opens PR today, CI sweep, canary tomorrow morning. Ciara will own the telemetry schema, I'll push the console copy update.
Deploy Bot: matcher-service v1.12.3-canary queued by Alex
Maya: :thumbsup:
